description: I'm Jagan, join my team and let's build some valuable stuffs.
summary:
FireCalendar helps users explore satellite-detected fire activity over a selected area and time period. MODIS and VIIRS observe fires at different spatial resolutions, so raw hotspot counts from the two sensors are not directly comparable. FireCalendar harmonizes VIIRS detections toward MODIS-equivalent units to create a more consistent time series.

Users can select an area of interest, date range, sensor and confidence settings, then view mapped hotspots, monthly and annual activity, seasonal patterns, historical comparisons, peak periods, trends and validation results. The app supports NASA FIRMS data, CSV/ZIP uploads and a synthetic demo for offline testing. It estimates uncertainty for VIIRS-derived monthly values and shows sensor calibration and cross-validation diagnostics.

FireCalendar is intended to help researchers, land managers and emergency planners examine historical burning patterns and identify periods for closer attention. Satellite detections and estimates have limitations and should support, not replace, official alerts or local response guidance.
details:
FireCalendar addresses a challenge in long-term active-fire monitoring: MODIS and VIIRS detections have different spatial resolutions and sensitivities, so their raw hotspot counts cannot be compared directly. A change in sensor coverage can therefore look like a change in burning activity.

The app lets users define an area of interest using a bounding box, point and radius, or GeoJSON/KML, and choose a date range, historical baseline, sensor mode and confidence threshold. It supports NASA FIRMS ingestion modes, CSV/ZIP upload and a synthetic demo. The app maps detections and provides calendar, monthly and annual trend views, seasonal summaries, historical comparisons, peak-period tables and validation charts.

For harmonization, the app describes snapping VIIRS detections to an equal-area 1 km grid, applying day/night fire-radiative-power thresholds, calibrating newer VIIRS satellites against MODIS during overlap years with a log-link GLM, and using year-block bootstrapping to estimate prediction intervals. Validation views include leave-one-year-out metrics and residual-agreement plots.

Cloud cover, smoke, viewing angle, satellite overpass timing and provisional near-real-time data can affect detections. VIIRS-only estimates may have wider uncertainty. The built-in Sierra Nevada demo uses deterministic synthetic data for testing; its counts and trends are not observed fire activity. FireCalendar supports analysis and planning but does not predict fire starts or replace official alerts. The app uses NASA FIRMS active-fire data and displays map attribution to OpenStreetMap and Leaflet.
